title: RAIDERS trial in Kigali, Rwanda: immediate Cybersight AI results raise referral uptake for diabetic retinopathy from 39.6% to 51.5%
summary: In the RAIDERS trial at four Kigali diabetes clinics, immediate Cybersight AI feedback raised 30-day referral attendance to 51.5% from 39.6% with delayed human grading.
account: Orbis International and the Rwanda International Institute of Ophthalmology ran the RAIDERS randomized trial at four diabetes clinics in and around Kigali, Rwanda. Screening ran from March to June 2021, and follow-up continued through July 2021. Retinal images went to Cybersight AI, a grading service that Orbis offers free to eye health professionals in low- and middle-income countries and that returns a result within 60 seconds. The 275 adults whom the AI judged to need referral were randomly assigned to receive the AI result and referral advice at once or to receive referral advice after human grading three to five days later. Within 30 days, 70 of 136 people (51.5%) in the immediate group attended the referral service, against 55 of 139 (39.6%) in the delayed group (P = 0.048). The trial was small and short. Several authors are employees of Orbis, which provides the AI service.
purpose: Cybersight AI was built to grade retinal images for referable diabetic retinopathy. In this trial its immediate result let clinics advise referral on the day of screening; the higher referral uptake was the purpose of that use.
deployer: Orbis International with the Rwanda International Institute of Ophthalmology, at four diabetes clinics

ratings.reason: 51.5% of people told their AI result at once attended referral services within 30 days against 39.6% of those told after human grading.

ai_role.statement: People who needed referral were randomly assigned to immediate AI feedback or to delayed human grading, so the difference in uptake is attributable to the immediate AI result.

evidence.citation: Leigh JA, Sherrington A, Barber ARJ, Turner AW, Kidd M, Powell J, Pope C. Referral uptake after diabetic retinopathy screening with artificial intelligence-assisted care pathways: a systematic review and meta-analysis. NPJ Digit Med. 2026;9:468. doi:10.1038/s41746-026-02616-3
evidence.title: Referral uptake after diabetic retinopathy screening with artificial intelligence-assisted care pathways: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.quote: Mathenge et al.'s RAIDERS RCT ( n = 275) uniquely isolated the effect of immediate versus delayed feedback by randomising patients to immediate AI result acquisition with a colour-coded report based upon severity, or delayed manual grading (3-5 days) with SMS and phone calls to flag results, finding 51.5% versus 39.6% referral uptake respectively

evidence.citation: Mathenge W, Whitestone N, Nkurikiye J, et al. Impact of Artificial Intelligence Assessment of Diabetic Retinopathy on Referral Service Uptake in a Low-Resource Setting: The RAIDERS Randomized Trial. Ophthalmol Sci. 2022;2(4):100168. doi:10.1016/j.xops.2022.100168
evidence.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence Assessment of Diabetic Retinopathy on Referral Service Uptake in a Low-Resource Setting: The RAIDERS Randomized Trial
evidence.quote: Referral adherence was statistically significantly higher in the intervention group (70/136 [51.5%]) versus the control group (55/139 [39.6%]; P = 0.048), a 30.1% increase.

produced_by: The AI returned a grade within 60 seconds of image upload.
Clinic staff gave referral advice on the day of screening.
The comparison was referral advice three to five days later after human grading.
must_hold: Clinics need an internet connection to reach the AI service.
Referral services must be reachable for the people referred.
